- When sentiment is positive (≥0.3) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and forecast is trending up, lower the forecast by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, the model tends to overcorrect — adjust downward by 2–4% in the next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5) and forecast is erratic, smooth the curve by averaging 3–5 consecutive points to reduce noise.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true values by 2–4% over 10+ days, apply a 1–2% downward bias to future 30d forecasts.  
- For high sentiment + high recent prices, model often overreacts — cap forecast at 10% below recent 5-day high to avoid overbought bias.
